cf.title: Fix a file descriptor leak when using io_method=io_uring

input.subject: [Bug Report + Patch] File descriptor leak when io_method=io_uring

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated with a reproduction, several reviewers confirmed the leak, and the fix follows the existing pgaio_worker_die() pattern in method_worker.c. A committer reports the v1-based fix pushed to master and 18, which leaves IoMethodOps unchanged. Confidence is medium because only 3 of 22 messages and no code were read.

brief.title: Close io_uring rings in the postmaster on crash restart
brief.problem: With io_method=io_uring, the postmaster never releases its io_uring instances, so each crash restart after a killed backend doubles the io_uring fd count. Repeated crashes, or one crash with large max_connections, can then stop the restart with "Too many open files" or "Cannot allocate memory", and the server shuts down. Postgres 18 and master are affected.
brief.proposed_design: v1 registers an on_shmem_exit() callback in pgaio_uring_shmem_init() that calls io_uring_queue_exit() for each ring, following pgaio_worker_die() in method_worker.c. v2 to v4 instead add a shmem_cleanup callback to IoMethodOps, registered in AioShmemInit(). The committer used a revised v1 for master and REL_18_STABLE, and reports it pushed.
user_visible_surface: C API: new shmem_cleanup member of IoMethodOps in the installed server header aio_internal.h (v2 to v4 only, not in the committed v1-based fix).
Server log: the restart no longer fails with "could not setup io_uring queue: Too many open files" after crash restarts.
author_claims: The leak reproduces on Postgres 18.0 to 18.3 and master, on kernels 6.8 to 6.19 with liburing 2.5 to 2.13.
Only the postmaster runs the callback, because child processes reset the postmaster's exit callbacks.
v3 and v4 break the Postgres 18 ABI if backpatched, because the new field sits in the middle of IoMethodOps.
The author first hit the bug through ulimit -l, which gave "Cannot allocate memory" at restart.
brief.thread_state: Several reviewers confirmed the leak and the fix, and Fujii Masao reports he pushed the v1-based patch to master and 18. Still open is a follow-up so cleanup uses postmaster-local copies of ring descriptors, since shared memory may be corrupted; Fujii Masao's draft depends on liburing internals.
unclear: The commit hash and the exact branches that got the fix are not stated.
The thread does not say whether the shmem_cleanup interface will still go into master.
For the follow-up, the thread does not say if liburing allows passing a copied struct io_uring to io_uring_queue_exit().
No regression test for the leak across crash restart is mentioned.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: v2 to v4 add a shmem_cleanup member to IoMethodOps in aio_internal.h; the committed v1-based fix does not.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The fix targets REL_18_STABLE; v3 and v4 would break the Postgres 18 ABI, so the v1 shape was used.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The postmaster now calls io_uring_queue_exit() at crash restart, and the planned follow-up depends on liburing internals.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which commit and which branches carry the fix, so the CommitFest entry can be closed as committed?
Does liburing allow io_uring_queue_exit() on a postmaster-local copy of struct io_uring, or does the follow-up need another way to keep the ring descriptors?
Can a test kill a backend with io_method=io_uring and check that the postmaster's io_uring fd count stays the same after the crash restart?
Will the shmem_cleanup member of IoMethodOps still be proposed for master, and which second IO method would use it?

committability.owner_note: Fujii Masao is listed as committer on the CommitFest entry and reports the v1-based fix pushed. The follow-up needs someone who knows the AIO io_uring code and postmaster crash restart.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the postmaster's exit and crash-restart path with io_method=io_uring on master and 18, including cleanup that reads ring descriptors from shared memory a crashed backend may have corrupted, until the follow-up lands.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 to v4 after review and set the entry back to Needs review on 2026-09-09, so the author stays engaged.

priority.reason: The fix is a small change in one file for a confirmed leak that can stop a crash restart with io_method=io_uring, and it is reported pushed. What remains is to close the entry and review the follow-up for postmaster-local ring descriptors as a separate patch.

provisional_note: The code and messages #4 to #22 were not read, so the callback's behaviour in the postmaster and the pushed commit could not be checked. The follow-up that depends on liburing internals was not judged.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: s/shm_mq_iovec/struct iovec/
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace the shm_mq module's own shm_mq_iovec struct with the standard POSIX struct iovec. The motivation was to remove a duplicate definition now that struct iovec can be used everywhere.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas argued that the two structs belong to separate APIs and should stay separate. Reusing struct iovec could tie shm_mq to POSIX limits such as IOV_MAX, and it would stop shm_mq from adding its own fields later. The author accepted this and marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
They serve a similar purpose,
but they belong to completely separate APIs; I think "incidental
deduplication" is the right term for that.

precedents_retrieved.title: Asynchronous and "direct" IO support for PostgreSQL
precedents_retrieved.authors: Andres Freund (andresfreund), David Rowley (davidrowley), Thomas Munro (macdice)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Andres Freund proposed an asynchronous IO (AIO) subsystem for Postgres, with several backends (worker processes, io_uring, posix AIO, Windows) and helpers for streaming reads and writes. The same work adds optional direct IO, so data moves between storage and shared buffers without the kernel page cache.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry died of inactivity. The patch set stopped applying in January 2022 and no rebased version followed. In May 2022 Aleksander Alekseev asked for a rebase and said a set of 39 patches was too large to review, and that it should be split. Michael Paquier marked it Returned with feedback after five months without activity.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don't know what's the exact status here, but as there has been no
activity for the past five months, I have just marked the entry as RwF
for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: Show WAL stats on pg_stat_io
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds WAL I/O (writes, fsyncs, reads during recovery, and WAL segment initialization in a new IOCONTEXT_INIT) to the pg_stat_io view as IOOBJECT_WAL. Timings use track_wal_io_timing, and pg_stat_wal timings would come from pg_stat_io.
precedents_retrieved.objection: pg_stat_io ties op_bytes to a fixed block size per object and context, but some WAL reads, such as those by the WAL receiver, have a variable size. Reviewers did not agree whether to set op_bytes to 1, to NULL, or to add per-operation byte columns. Michael Paquier proposed to set the patch aside until WAL reads and writes, async I/O and cached reads are settled, so that the meaning of pg_stat_io does not change between releases. The author agreed, and the patch was marked Returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IMHO, perhaps we'd better put this patch aside until we are absolutely
*sure* of what we want to achieve when it comes to WAL, and I am
afraid that this cannot happen until we're happy with the way we
handle WAL reads *and* writes, including WAL receiver or anything that
has the idea of pulling its own page callback with
XLogReaderAllocate() in the backend.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix Deadlock Issue in Single User Mode When IO Failure Occurs
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a hang in single-user mode when a relation read or write fails during startup recovery or a checkpoint: AbortBufferIO() at process exit waits on a buffer I/O lwlock that the process still holds. It makes sure all lwlocks are released before AbortBufferIO() runs, first by registering LWLockReleaseAll() as an exit callback and in v3 by calling it in AtProcExit_Buffers().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila tested the create table, insert and checkpoint repro and reported that the patch does not fix the problem. The second I/O error, raised during ShutdownXLOG() at exit, now ends in an assertion failure in UnpinBuffer() called from ReleaseAuxProcessResources. Michael Paquier reproduced the same trace and asked the author for an update, but the author did not respond, so the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I have tried to look into this patch and I don't think it fixes the
problem.

precedents_retrieved.title: Row Level Security, leakproof-ness, and performance implications
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread started from slow queries under row-level security, caused by many built-in operator functions not being marked leakproof, and a patch marked enum_eq, enum_ne, textin and textout leakproof. Later proposals were a documentation patch listing RLS restrictions on the CREATE POLICY page, and Joe Conway's idea to redact error messages sent to clients plus a GUC to treat all functions as leakproof.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut wrote that redacting error messages had been found not to satisfy the leakproofness criteria, and Joe Conway accepted that the consensus was against him. Robert Haas suggested doing it outside core, with a logging hook and functions marked leakproof by hand, and doubted that customers could be supported with redacted messages. Peter also found the CREATE POLICY page the wrong place for the documentation patch and asked how a list of non-leakproof operators would be kept complete. The visible messages do not show which of these two patches this entry is.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think that approach has been found not to actually satisfy the leakproofness criteria.

precedents_retrieved.title: Function to track shmem reinit time
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Tomas Vondra, Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a function pg_shmem_init_time() that returns when shared memory was last initialized or reinitialized, so monitoring tools can detect crash restarts under restart_after_crash without parsing the server log. A second small patch removes dead shared memory reinit code and fixes comments in postmaster.c.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers doubted the premise. Tom Lane argued that the time of the last crash says little about how often crashes happen, and that improving the log would matter more. Tomas Vondra showed that comparing the value to pg_postmaster_start_time fails because the two come from separate timestamp calls, and Peter Eisentraut objected to a name that exposes shared memory internals. The patch also stopped applying after commit fd1a421fe, and the entry was returned with feedback with no new version posted; Robert Haas later spoke in favour and suggested an out-of-core extension.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think that if we're to do anything in this area,
improving the usefulness of the log would be more important than
providing the proposed function.

precedents_retrieved.title: Function to track shmem reinit time
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Peter Eisentraut, Tomas Vondra
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a function pg_shmem_init_time() that returns when shared memory was last initialized or reinitialized, so monitoring tools can detect crash restarts without parsing logs. A second patch removes dead shared memory reinit code in postmaster.c.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the function exposes an implementation detail that may change, and that frequent crashes should be fixed, not measured. Earlier, Peter Eisentraut objected to the shmem-based name, and Tomas Vondra argued that comparing with pg_postmaster_start_time does not reliably detect restarts. Robert Haas and Alexander Korotkov supported it, and David Steele returned the entry because the discussion stayed at an impasse.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
(1) it's exposing an implementation detail that clients should not be
concerned with, and that we might change in future.

precedents_retrieved.title: Do not exit on postmaster death event inside CRIT sections.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes a process that detects postmaster death inside WaitEventSetWait defer its exit while it is in a critical section, and exit only after the section ends. The goal was to stop proc_exit(1) from releasing LWLocks mid-change, which let the checkpointer flush a modified buffer whose WAL record was never written.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that deferring exit leads to systems that fail to shut down. The author then confirmed that the checkpointer waits forever in LWLockAcquire in the test. Tom also argued that proc_exit(1) after postmaster death is the real defect, and that removing the death check is as hazardous as keeping it this late in the v18 cycle. The thread instead reverted commit bc22dc0e0, which had started using condition variables inside critical sections, and left better postmaster-death handling to a new thread.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I do not like this patch one bit: it will replace one set of problems with another set, namely systems that fail to shut down.

precedents_retrieved.title: In INSERT/UPDATE, use the table's real tuple descriptor as target.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
In INSERT/UPDATE, use the table's real tuple descriptor as target.
Reverted commit(s): Fix corner case for a BEFORE ROW UPDATE trigger returning OLD.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Previously, ExecInitModifyTable relied on ExecInitJunkFilter,
and thence ExecCleanTypeFromTL, to build the target descriptor from
the query tlist.  While we just checked (in ExecCheckPlanOutput)
that the tlist produces compatible output, this is not a great
substitute for the relation's actual tuple descriptor that's
available from the relcache.  For one thing, dropped columns will
not be correctly marked attisdropped; it's a bit surprising that
we've gotten away with that this long.  But the real reason for
being concerned with this is that using the table's descriptor means
that the slot will have correct attrmissing data, allowing us to
revert the klugy fix of commit ba9f18abd.  (This commit undoes
that one's changes in trigger.c, but keeps the new test case.)
Thus we can solve the bogus-trigger-tuple problem with fewer cycles
rather than more.

No back-patch, since this doesn't fix any additional bug, and it
seems somewhat more likely to have unforeseen side effects than
ba9f18abd's narrow fix.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no earlier attempt at this idea, and the thread does not point to an earlier discussion of it. Several reviewers confirmed the bug fix and a committer reports it pushed (message #18), so a prior-attempts objection has nothing to stand on.

The fix adds no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog object, dump state or psql behaviour, and the only change users see is that crash restarts now succeed. The one compatibility risk, the IoMethodOps ABI break in v3 and v4, was settled in messages #9, #12 and #14 when the committer chose the v1-based fix, which leaves the struct unchanged, for master and 18.

The fix changes no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, replication or wire-protocol state; it only releases postmaster-local io_uring fds at crash restart. The committed v1 shape leaves IoMethodOps unchanged, so the v18 ABI is safe. The risk of trusting ring descriptors in shared memory that a crashing backend may have corrupted was raised in message #16, and a follow-up is in progress (messages #17 and #21).

The fix adds no new privileges and exposes no data; message #10 shows the leaked ring fds are FD_CLOEXEC and so never reach COPY FROM PROGRAM or untrusted PL children. The postmaster's use of ring descriptors from shared memory (message #16) needs prior memory corruption, gains no privilege, and is already tracked as a follow-up.

This is a small bug fix for a real crash-restart failure, and a committer has already pushed it to master and 18. From the maintenance angle it adds no hot-path cost, no new API in the committed form, and no new external dependency beyond the existing liburing calls. The open follow-up for postmaster-local ring descriptors, which depends on liburing internals, is a separate proposal and should be judged when it is posted.

No existing feature does the job. Postgres has no way to release io_uring instances in the postmaster across a crash restart, so the server can fail to restart. The fix reuses the existing on_shmem_exit() pattern from method_worker.c and adds no second mechanism. An extension or hook cannot fix a leak inside core AIO setup.

The leak is a confirmed bug fix, not a feature. Four reviewers reproduced it on several kernels, and message #10 shows one crash with max_connections = 1000 stops the server. The author hit it in production (message #12), so demand is not in question.
